summary: A Baytech Plastics web page explaining how quality plastic manufacturers monitor production quality in injection molding. It covers the goal of quality control (monitoring samples against tolerances), six common injection molding defects, measures such as setpoint tolerances, machine data and trained inspection staff, and the importance of a clean assembly environment. The page closes by promoting Baytech Plastics as an Ontario manufacturer with over 70 years of experience.
one_line: Explains quality control methods and common injection molding defects used by plastic manufacturers, promoting Baytech Plastics of Midland, Ontario.
key_facts: Quality plastic manufacturers use a variety of quality control strategies that guarantee high levels of customer satisfaction and eliminate costly mistakes.
The goal of quality control is to monitor samples to assess whether critical measures are outside the bounds of tolerance while production schedules move forward.
Parameters such as color, texture, and size should be assessed to see whether cavity pressure, injection time, injection speed, and cooling time need adjusting before all parts are molded.
Sink Marks are indentations that may appear if the outer wall of a part solidifies and compacts quickly while the inner layer is still hot and fluid.
Gas Marks result from air vents at incorrect depth, which prevents air from exiting when plastic is shot into the cavity, causing burn marks.
Flashes are thin protrusions of plastic that leak out of a mold if the two sides do not come together tightly enough.
Short Shots occur when too little plastic is injected, so an injection mold won't fill properly.
Weld Lines occur where plastic flows around a hole in a part and create weak spots; Splays are surface blemishes caused by air bubbles trapped in the plastic.
Modern machinery can monitor mathematical parameters like fill speed, pack time, and pressure so defects can be minimized and eliminated.
Presses can deliver real-time data about production time, scrap, rejects, and parts created, but there is no substitute for a highly-trained staff with a critical eye.
Initial articles from the injection mold need to be inspected in fine detail, adjustments made, and subsequent runs inspected again.
Facilities need sufficient lighting and space, clearly-established contaminant handling procedures, and regular cleaning and maintenance.
Baytech Plastics claims over 70 years of experience and a strong commitment to innovation.
Baytech Plastics is located at 320 Elizabeth Street, Midland, ON, Canada L4R 4L6, with a general inquiries line at (705) 526-7801.
